summary_evidence.sync_counter_semantics: fallback_waits counts fallback sleep iterations, not unique waits or a failure rate; direct/pipe counters count dispatch calls and wait durations overlap.

findings: IMMEDIATE presentation is confirmed with syncInterval=0, 1280x720, three swapchain images and LSFG off. Scheduler masks remain 7 and all recorded affinity operations succeed.

Current capture is 19.930 FPS (50.177 ms/frame); previous FIFO capture was 20.431 FPS (48.945 ms/frame). This supports the user's observation of no material additional gain, but the route and camera are uncontrolled.

Vulkan fence wall waits persist at 17.935 ms per call even under IMMEDIATE, versus 16.421 ms in the previous FIFO capture. The wait cannot therefore be treated as a removable one-refresh FIFO tax; no GPU execution timestamps or native-wait cause breakdown exist.

CPU work is now substantial: capture-adjacent registered usage is 2.32–2.65 cores. The main thread uses 46.9–53.7 percent of one core, DXVK-CS 40.8–46.6 percent, and three game workers 28.5–35.1 percent each. A low percentage for one thread or overall four-core display understates demand on the three automatic application cores.

The main thread performs 100,784 wine_event calls and each of workers 16/20/24 performs roughly 40,500 wine_select calls during capture, versus 56,696 and roughly 21,000 respectively in the prior FIFO capture. This identifies significant synchronization traffic; it does not establish its removable CPU cost or whether the different scene causes the increase.
Wine wait totals and Vulkan fence/semaphore waits are overlapping wall times. They cannot be summed as a serial frame cost or used as direct GPU utilization.

Compilation and storage activity occur in some windows, but seven of fourteen slow windows have zero pipeline creation and still remain near 20 FPS. Main-thread Sleep(0) wall time is small compared with total frame time; no sleep-related giant gap is evidenced.
